topic: A Breakaway Road Sign Support Is Designed to Release at Its Base
creativeBrief:
Pattern: CONTRADICTION_REVEAL_V4. Audience: global English-speaking viewers. Channel promise: surprising engineering hidden in recognizable objects. Generate five diverse declarative subject-first hooks, 5–10 spoken words preferred, 12 absolute maximum; opening display copy 2–5 words. The suggested hook is a candidate, not a pre-approved package. State only the supported result in the hook; save the physical explanation for mechanism. Keep the explicit titleSeed and descriptionSeed. The title is metadata, not a line to repeat in the story. Use six functions across five voiced scenes: visual paradox shares contradiction, then clue, mechanism, second_reveal, payoff. Protect fact consequence for the distinct second_reveal; do not disclose it in contradiction or clue. The clue adds a concrete observation rather than restating the hook. Target 25–29 seconds including the configured sign-off, hard maximum 30. Aim for 65–72 total spoken words including sign-off without padding. Mechanism begins at or after 7 seconds; second_reveal starts between 14 and 21 seconds. Each later scene must fit its measured used interval within a six-second source, including the incoming 0.2-second transition. Keep voice, distinct spoken/display copy, karaoke, local BGM and channel outro. No generic spoken CTA or dark wash. Generate five distinct Gemini first frames and matching Google Flow clips. The opening still already shows the recognizable subject and puzzling result. Use a different camera role per scene, varying at least two of scale, angle, setting and physical action between adjacent shots. Important action must finish inside the used interval, not just the six-second source. Generated media is explanatory illustration, never documentary evidence. Do not invent a crash, disaster, rescue, measurement or demonstration outcome. Use only facts below and respect all factBoundaries. Review the actual portrait crop and motion before binding local videos.

Editorial pilot condition: C: less familiar design detail, current packaging. Preserve the agreed title style; current-style controls should remain clear and accurate, not deliberately weak. Familiarity is an editorial hypothesis, not a measured popularity claim.

YouTube title seed: That Road Sign Has a Safety Feature You Missed
YouTube description seed: Some roadside signs use a base designed to release under impact. On the described slip-base design, overtightening can stop that release working properly. Have you noticed the bolted base beneath a roadside sign? #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts

Suggested opening hook: Some road signs are built to come apart.
Suggested opening display: Built to Come Apart
Select one meaningful emphasis token from the final opening display copy.

Scene development:
contradiction: show a recognizable small workshop model of a roadside guide-sign support with its upper slip-base plate already offset from the lower plate, the upper post held by the demonstration fixture. The separated end state and sign-panel context are visible in frame zero. This illustrates a release result, not a real crash; reserve sliding and hinge action for mechanism.
clue: a wider workshop view shows the same model in its assembled configuration, clearly establishing sign-panel context and the deliberate bolted connection. Keep its reference geometry unchanged; do not portray damage or expose the overtightening reveal.
mechanism: a clearly identifiable workshop model of the same reference slip-base design demonstrates how the base can separate while the upper support can rotate at its separate hinge. Do not imply the model demonstrates certified real crash performance.
second_reveal: fact consequence; static close view of the matching bolted base and a maintenance worker inspecting it. Explain that excessive base-plate tightening can prevent correct release. Do not show a torque value, instructions to loosen bolts, or a fabricated over-tightened crash.
payoff: return to the intact assembled sign support beside an ordinary road; describe release as an engineered feature, with correct maintenance as part of its operation.

Source-backed facts:
mechanism: FHWA describes large steel roadside sign supports with a slip base that can separate from the foundation under impact, allowing the post to rotate about a hinge below the sign panel.
consequence: TxDOT warns that overtightening the base plates on rectangular slip-base sign supports can prevent them breaking away properly.

Factual boundaries:
Explain the referenced U.S. rectangular slip-base steel-support family, not every road sign, pole or country’s installation.
A slip base, an upper hinge/fuse detail and a yielding or sleeve support are different components or designs. Choose one actual reference arrangement and preserve it; do not invent a hybrid.
Do not promise survival, harmless debris, safe passage in every collision or a numerical crash-performance result.
Do not stage a crash, rescue or real-world release as documentary footage. Any moving support is a clearly identifiable explanatory model.
The overtightening claim concerns the described base-plate connection, not every bolt. Give no torque specifications or public-road maintenance instructions.
Do not infer that a normal bolted sign is defective, loose or currently dangerous.
